answer: Imagine a lotus rooted on a knoll, never transplanted: each agent grows one lotus, and to prove it must recite a sonnet of fourteen lines, each line chained to the last by a memory-hard step no machine can rush or split across cores. A finished sonnet counts 14 squared = 196; fourteen newborn lotus count 14 in all, yet each still pays a full bond. One honest gardener keeps a single lotus and earns only what its own fourteen lines earned.
